title: HolisticMotion: Holistic Modeling for Motion Reconstruction from Sparse Tracking
description:
arXiv:2605.22631v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Reconstructing full-body motion from sparse tracking signals is crucial for immersive AR/VR applications. Existing methods predominantly adopt a sensor-centric observation perspective, learning full-body representations primarily under sparse conditioning, while additional joint observations available during training remain underutilized as inputs. We propose HolisticMotion, which shifts the modeling perspective toward holistic full-body modeling by treating every joint as a potential input source within a unified skeletal layout. Guided by this holistic perspective, we introduce three complementary designs. First, a curriculum masking strategy bridges full-body motion learning and sparse inference by gradually shifting training from a mixture of masked full-body and sparse inputs to exclusively sparse inputs. Second, body partitioning models region dynamics and helps preserve local motion cues. Third, Kinematic Attention coordinates body regions by combining dynamic spatial interactions with learnable structural priors inspired by the kinematic tree. Experiments on AMASS and HPS demonstrate competitive reconstruction performance across various tracking protocols, with the lowest positional errors among the compared methods. The unified representation also accommodates additional wearable sensors, yielding further improvements in reconstruction accuracy and motion smoothness.
